F1.title: The Exits table never names option-shaping, the one chain member between its `ideate` and `making-recommendations` rows
F1.detail: The Exits table (SKILL.md:83-92) has no row for the reachable state where two or more options are named but sketch-level or unevenly understood — the entry condition of `option-shaping`, a sibling in the same plugin. The word `option-shaping` appears nowhere in the outcome-shaping subtree (SKILL.md, agents/openai.yaml, examples/interaction-examples.md). The two rows that bracket the case exclude it by their own wording: `making-recommendations` requires options "clear enough to compare" (SKILL.md:86) and `ideate` requires a field "too thin to want anything yet" (SKILL.md:87). Both targets refuse it in their own contracts: `ideate` says "Do not use to develop a fixed sketch-level field to comparable depth (`option-shaping`)", and `making-recommendations`' Field Readiness is a hard stop — "name `option-shaping`, say which options are materially underdeveloped or uneven, ask to develop the entire fixed field first, and stop. A direct request for a pick does not waive this stop." So the agent either burns a handoff hop that the downstream lane is obliged to bounce, or fills an uneven field inside making-recommendations against that lane's own rule. The state is not exotic: outcome-shaping's own missing-options handling tells the agent to "Offer two or three sharply contrasting concretes to react to" (SKILL.md:34), which puts a sketch-level field on the table from inside this lane, and the 2026-07-02 first-live-fire record confirms that is what happened. This reads as drift, not a drawn boundary: outcome-shaping's table was written 2026-07-02 (26d7ae9), `option-shaping` landed 2026-07-13 (fc7e7a0), and the table was edited again 2026-09-01 (3da8e35, adding the to-questionnaire row) without backfilling. README.md:14 asserts the property that fails here — "The forward chain is `outcome-shaping` → `ideate` → `option-shaping` → `making-recommendations`... Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary" — and every other chain member does name it.
F1.evidence: SKILL.md:83-92 Exits table (design-exploration, making-recommendations, ideate, prototype, to-questionnaire, grill-me, review, closure — no option-shaping row); `grep -rn "option-shaping" plugins/decide/skills/outcome-shaping/` returns nothing. SKILL.md:86 "Criteria and two or more serious options are clear enough to compare"; SKILL.md:87 "The field of options is too thin to want anything yet"; SKILL.md:34 "Offer two or three sharply contrasting concretes to react to". making-recommendations/SKILL.md Field Readiness: "name `option-shaping`... and stop. A direct request for a pick does not waive this stop." ideate/SKILL.md:3 "Do not use to develop a fixed sketch-level field to comparable depth (`option-shaping`)". README.md:14 forward-chain claim. git: fc7e7a0 2026-07-13 (option-shaping added), 26d7ae9 2026-07-02 and 3da8e35 2026-09-01 (outcome-shaping SKILL.md).
F1.proposed_fix: Add one Exits row between the making-recommendations and ideate rows: "| Two or more options are named but sketch-level or unevenly understood | `option-shaping` |", placed so the readiness distinction is visible in reading order. Leave the frontmatter description unchanged: it is already ~81 words against the ~90 cap and option-shaping guards that direction itself (one source argued for adding it there too).

F2.title: The one write outcome-shaping permits is unspecified in the skill and unaccounted for in the plugin's published privacy notice
F2.detail: SKILL.md:107 permits a write and then says nothing about it: "briefs are chat-only: write a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks." When the user does ask, the agent must improvise what the artifact is (the capsule? a longer brief?), where it goes, and whether it gets committed. Every other write-capable lane in this plugin fixes all three: `design-exploration` ("place it per repo convention, asking one path question if no convention is clear. Do not commit automatically"), `decision-record` (`docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` plus a named local commit), `deliberate` (a capsule file only on request), and the neighbor `to-questionnaire` ("Leave the artifact uncommitted for the user. Never commit on a protected or default branch."). The silence has a concrete consequence for this user: the global always-loaded Markdown auto-commit rule stages and commits Markdown created at the user's request in a git worktree, and it yields only to "a governing skill's explicit instruction about its own writes" — outcome-shaping states none, so a shaping brief is auto-committed while a design doc from the sibling lane is explicitly not, a divergence inside one plugin decided by omission. Separately, the plugin's published privacy notice denies the write can exist: PRIVACY.md:7 enumerates every write (`design-exploration`'s approved document, `deliberate`'s run store and on-request capsule, `decision-record`'s ADR plus commit) and closes "nothing else on disk", then says "Three paths can carry content off this machine" naming only `making-recommendations`, `deliberate`, and `scope-cut` — outcome-shaping's user-requested *ticket* is an unnamed fourth off-machine path. This is not an omitted default: PRIVACY already accounts for other on-request writes, so on-request writes are inside its model, and README.md's Storage row carries the carve-out while PRIVACY does not. plugin.json:42's `privacyPolicyURL` points at this document, so the understatement is published. Corroborating drift in the same PRIVACY sentence: it still describes decision-record's supersession write as only "a `Status` line on the superseded record", which 1.2.0 widened to also allow a dated amendment section (README Storage row; CHANGELOG.md:11).

Three paths can carry content off this machine, each under the user's control..." | README.md Storage, outcome-shaping row: "Nothing. Chat-only; a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks." | design-exploration/SKILL.md Artifacts: "place it per repo convention... Do not commit automatically." | skills/to-questionnaire/SKILL.md: "Leave the artifact uncommitted for the user." | ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md Markdown auto-commit: "A governing skill's explicit instruction about its own writes overrides this default." | plugin.json:42 privacyPolicyURL.
F2.proposed_fix: Two one-clause edits. In The Capsule, say what the requested artifact is and how it behaves: the capsule is the brief; place it per repo convention, asking one path question when none is clear; leave it uncommitted for the user. In PRIVACY.md:7, add outcome-shaping's on-request write to the enumeration so "nothing else on disk" stays true, and either name the user-requested ticket as a fourth off-machine path or reword to "Content can leave this machine on these paths" so the count stops needing maintenance. While in that sentence, refresh the stale decision-record supersession description.

F3.title: outcome-check declares outcome-shaping the source of its goal metric, but the capsule has no observable beat and never persists
F3.detail: `outcome-check` binds itself to this lane in three places — "Closes the loop `outcome-shaping` opens" (frontmatter and body), and "It *opens* the goal loop up front... `outcome-check` *closes* it, after the ship" — and sources its first move from it: "**Name the goal metric** — the one the change existed to move. Pull it from the source: the original clarified outcome (`outcome-shaping`), the `acceptance-map` check IDs, the PR or issue. Do not invent it." That named source does not exist on either axis. Content: the capsule's six beats are settled / open / leaning / binding constraints and accepted trades / ruled out / next move (SKILL.md:100-106) — none asks what would show the want was met, and nothing in The Read, Type the Mud, or Load-Testing the Want elicits an observable. Durability: the capsule is chat-only by contract (SKILL.md:107), so months later there is no artifact, and in a fresh session no conversation either — the other two sources outcome-check names are durable artifacts. The consequence is bounded but real: outcome-check's empty-case fallback is "If no goal was ever named, say so and route back to `outcome-shaping`", which weeks after the ship sends the user into a pre-decision interview lane to name a goal for a change that already shipped, next door to the thing outcome-check exists to forbid ("do not invent a goal so there is something to check"). So the cost is a search plus a bounce rather than a wrong verdict, but the paired claim is inaccurate as written and stated three times. The 2026-07-02 methodology critique already named this as the lane's one external check: "nothing in the method ever tests the clarified outcome against anything external... (`outcome-check` closes the loop eventually — but months later)."

F3.proposed_fix: Fix one side so the two stop disagreeing. Option A (content): add one optional capsule beat governed by the existing "Omit any beat with no real content rather than manufacture one" — what the user said would show this actually happened, in their words, only when one emerged; it is a want-shaped question, not a metric ritual, so it stays inside the lane's non-goals. Option B (durability): add one clause to the capsule paragraph naming survival past the session — for a later `outcome-check`, a ticket, or a handoff — as one of the explicit asks this lane will write for. Option C (the other side): soften outcome-check:18 to "a written outcome brief, if the shaping was captured to one".

F4.title: Three surfaces disagree on whether the lane may produce a recommendation itself or must hand off
F4.detail: Exits opens flatly: "This lane prepares; it does not design, decide, critique, or implement. When the work shifts, name the move and let the user decline" (SKILL.md:81), and Core Behavior states the invariant "hand off by name when the work shifts (see Exits)" (SKILL.md:24). Restraints says something different: "No verdicts, rankings, or settled recommendations; this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them" (SKILL.md:126) — which permits the lane to become a recommendation after asking. The examples file resolves the ambiguity in the permissive direction: in "Flight Named Once" the user says "just recommend something" and the modeled reply is "If you want the recommendation anyway, I'll make it. Which way?" (examples/interaction-examples.md:96-99) — no lane named, the recommendation offered in-lane. The deference itself is deliberate (SKILL.md:77, name-once-then-comply, chosen in answer to the 2026-07-02 methodology critique's flight-into-health finding), so this is not a challenge to complying; the defect is that the three surfaces do not agree on what complying means. An agent following the example produces a recommendation without any of `making-recommendations`' guards — lean registration, field readiness, the runner-up's case — which is the machinery the plugin arc exists to supply, while README.md:14 claims each member "stops at its boundary".
F4.evidence: SKILL.md:81 "it does not design, decide, critique, or implement" vs SKILL.md:126 "this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them" vs examples/interaction-examples.md:96-99 "If you want the recommendation anyway, I'll make it." | SKILL.md:24 (hand off by name) | SKILL.md:86 (Exits row for making-recommendations) | README.md:14.
F4.proposed_fix: Pick one meaning and make all three say it. The cheapest version that keeps the deference: change the example's line to name the lane it complies through ("If you want the recommendation anyway, that's `making-recommendations` — I'll take us there. Which way?"), and reword Restraints:126 from "asks before becoming them" to "names the lane that owns them and asks before switching".

F5.title: An in-lane recommendation given at the flight moment carries no seam-marking, because the capsule fires only at handoffs
F5.detail: The user fleeing an uncomfortable trade and saying "just recommend something" is a documented, deliberately accepted input: SKILL.md:77 says name it once, gently, "then comply with whatever they choose. Deference with eyes open." The boundary is not the defect; what "comply" carries is. Restraints:126 permits an in-lane recommendation and the examples file commits to it outright, while the Exits row that would route it instead requires "Criteria and two or more serious options are clear enough to compare" (SKILL.md:86) — precisely what is not true at the flight moment, so the in-lane path is the reachable one. On that path every instrument that would mark the recommendation as resting on an unsettled want is inoperative: the capsule is the only place the skill requires marking "what the user confirmed in their own words versus what is still your compression", and it fires only "At a handoff point, or when the user asks to summarize" (SKILL.md:98). An in-lane recommendation is neither. So the agent produces a recommendation built on a want that failed the priced trade, with rival reads still live, and nothing in the text requires it to say so — the skill's own named hazard ("a crisp wrong read is more convincing than a true muddy one") realized at the moment the skill identifies as most dangerous. The 2026-07-02 live-fire record notes the instrument is still unexercised: "Flight-named-once / evidence testimony — unexercised."
F5.evidence: SKILL.md:77 "then comply with whatever they choose. Deference with eyes open." | SKILL.md:126 "No verdicts, rankings, or settled recommendations; this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them." | SKILL.md:98 "At a handoff point, or when the user asks to summarize, close with a short prose capsule" | SKILL.md:100 seam-marking beat | SKILL.md:86 exit precondition | examples/interaction-examples.md:97-99.
F5.proposed_fix: In the flight paragraph, say what compliance carries: a recommendation given inside this lane names, in one sentence, the trade that went unpriced and the rival read still live, so it travels with its own seam. Alternatively bind the capsule's seam-marking beat to this exit too, not only to handoffs and summarize requests.

F7.title: Type the Mud's missing-information routes omit the to-questionnaire exit the table carries
F7.detail: Type the Mud is the section that decides where non-interview-soluble mud goes, and its missing-information bullet names only impersonal evidence routes: "Name the evidence that would settle it and route toward it — a throwaway `prototype`, an experiment, a measurement" (SKILL.md:35). The Exits table carries a route that bullet does not: "The blocking unknown is knowledge only one named person can close → `to-questionnaire`" (SKILL.md:89). Knowledge held by a named colleague is missing-information mud, so an agent doing its mud-typing mid-interview — which the skill tells it to keep doing, "Re-type as you go" (SKILL.md:38) — has a three-item route list in front of it that sends a person-shaped unknown to a prototype or a measurement. This is drift from a deliberate fold: the to-questionnaire row was added 2026-09-01 (fold B3, commit 3da8e35) as a table row only, without touching the mud-typing routes it belongs to.

F8.title: The to-questionnaire exit is written as an operative hand-off to a skill the agent cannot invoke, against the library's stated user-invoked convention
F8.detail: The Exits row "The blocking unknown is knowledge only one named person can close | `to-questionnaire`" (SKILL.md:89) sits under "When the work shifts, name the move and let the user decline" (SKILL.md:81) and "When the user accepts a handoff, carry the capsule (below)" (SKILL.md:94). But `to-questionnaire` carries `disable-model-invocation: true`: on Claude Code only the human typing its token can start it, so "the user accepts the handoff" cannot be honored by the agent. The library states the rule for exactly this case in `agent-facing-design`, Library Conventions: "No skill can reach a user-invoked skill — a step whose precondition is one is phrased as an instruction for the human to run it (`/x` or `$x`), never as an operative invocation." The row is phrased as an operative hand-off and gives no token. `work-router` shows the compliant form for the same class of skill: "It is explicit-token-only (`/deliberate` or `$deliberate`) and hidden from model-side skill lists by design, so name the token in the route." The concrete outcome is a handoff the user accepts and nothing happens, or an agent that stalls having named a lane it cannot enter and cannot tell the user how to enter. The row landed 2026-09-01 (fold B3), with the convention already in force, and it is the only user-invoked destination in the table, so the fix is one row, not a policy change.

F8.proposed_fix: Rewrite the row's destination as a human instruction with its token — "`to-questionnaire` — the user runs `/to-questionnaire` (`$to-questionnaire`)" — or, if the cell is too narrow, put the qualification in the sentence under the table alongside the capsule instruction. F9.title: The ideate exit hands ideate the state ideate's own description declines, so the handoff bounces
F9.detail: outcome-shaping hands to `ideate` when "The field of options is too thin to want anything yet" (SKILL.md:87), and Type the Mud defines that state as "Missing options — they cannot want what they have not seen" (SKILL.md:34) — that is, the want is not formed yet. `ideate`'s own routing text declines exactly that: "Do not use to... clarify a still-muddy goal (`outcome-shaping`)" (ideate/SKILL.md:3), its first move is "If the *goal* is too muddy to say what would even count as an option, hand to `outcome-shaping`" (ideate/SKILL.md:14), and its when-not-to-widen list repeats it (ideate/SKILL.md:40). On a reachable input — a user who can name a dissatisfaction but neither a want nor a candidate — outcome-shaping hands off and ideate hands straight back. Neither surface states the discriminator that would break the bounce: ideate needs a frame it can generate against even while the want is unformed, so the handoff is right only once outcome-shaping can hand that frame over.

F9.proposed_fix: Add the frame condition to the Exits row so the handoff carries what ideate needs: "The field of options is too thin to want anything yet, and you can state the frame to generate against → `ideate`"; and in the Type-the-Mud missing-options bullet, make offering two or three concretes the move when that frame cannot yet be stated.

F10.title: No rule for the read surviving context compaction, so the capsule's own-words seam becomes unverifiable in exactly the long conversations the lane produces
F10.detail: The read is the lane's only carrier of state and it is rewrite-only: "one compact, evolving statement of the want... Rewrite it as understanding improves; never append a ledger" (SKILL.md:19). Everything else that matters lives in the raw transcript — the user's verbatim restatement ("That sentence — theirs, not yours — is the settled shape, and it goes into the capsule verbatim"), the trades accepted, the exclusions confirmed. Both runtimes this plugin ships to compact long conversations. After a compaction event mid-shaping the agent no longer holds the user's exact words, only a summary of them, yet the capsule beat still demands "what is settled, marking the seam honestly: what the user confirmed in their own words versus what is still your compression" (SKILL.md:100). Post-compaction that distinction cannot be drawn, and the agent has no way to notice it cannot: rewrite-only means a constraint confirmed at turn 2 and compressed out of the read by turn 12 leaves no trace to miss. The failure is silent and lands on the one artifact the contract says steers the next lane (SKILL.md:94). The same plugin proves the state is foreseeable and addressable — `deliberate`'s spine carries "After compaction, re-derive the fixed store locator, verify its echo, and rebuild exact packets and capsules from the store under freshly read references. Never use summarized memory for a compared value." outcome-shaping has no equivalent sentence, and grep across its subtree finds no mention of compaction or of a long-conversation state at all. It was flagged before the current body was written: the 2026-07-02 methodology critique says "rewrite-only plus lossy compaction means settled facts can evaporate without trace, and the capsule's 'what is settled' gets reconstructed from whatever survived." The rebuild folded most of that critique and not this.

Never use summarized memory for a compared value." | grep for "compact|compaction" across skills/outcome-shaping returns only the adjective "compact" describing the read | docs/reviews/2026-07-02-outcome-interviewer-methodology-critique.md §8 "No conservation law".
F10.proposed_fix: Add one fire-time sentence to Core Behavior or The Read covering the state, not a ledger: when the conversation has been compacted or has run long enough that you are working from a summary rather than the user's actual sentences, say so and re-confirm the settled shape in the user's words before any capsule, and mark anything you cannot source to their words as your compression. This fixes no new field and adds no beat.

F11.title: Parked and evidence-routed endings resume later by construction, but nothing carries the ripening condition or the settled shape past the session
F11.detail: Two of the lane's four documented endings resume later by definition. Parked: "the user is not ready. Name what would ripen it and stop" (SKILL.md:75) — the ripening condition is spoken once into chat and nothing else. Missing-information mud: "Name the evidence that would settle it and route toward it — a throwaway `prototype`, an experiment, a measurement" (SKILL.md:35), and the evidence arrives days or weeks later. In both cases the next session starts from nothing: the capsule is chat-only by contract (SKILL.md:107) and the skill's trigger is "a still-muddy idea", so the returning user re-enters at the beginning and re-shapes ground already covered, including the trades already priced and the exclusions already confirmed. No surface names a re-entry path — outcome-shaping never mentions `save-handoff`, `load-handoff`, or any durable route; `prototype`'s "When done" captures the answer and the question it answered, never the shaping read it came from, so the return leg carries evidence back to a lane that has forgotten the want. The gap is not the read-only boundary, which already permits a durable artifact on request and which this finding does not propose writing without a request; it is that at the two endings whose whole meaning is "resume later", nothing tells the agent to say the shape is about to be lost or to offer the route. The same plugin treats the identical problem as first-class one skill over: `scope-cut` gives every removed item "a re-entry condition, the observable that says 'pull this back in'" and routes the whole ledger to `triage`, while being just as chat-first. A parked want gets strictly less durability than a deferred ticket.
F11.evidence: SKILL.md:75 "**Parked** — the user is not ready. Name what would ripen it and stop." | SKILL.md:35 route to `prototype`/measurement | SKILL.md:107 "briefs are chat-only" | plugins/decide/skills/scope-cut/SKILL.md move 5: "Each carries a **re-entry condition**... Route the whole ledger to `/triage`" | skills/prototype/SKILL.md "When done" | grep across skills/outcome-shaping finds no save-handoff or cross-session route | docs/reviews/2026-07-02-outcome-shaping-first-live-fire.md, Open questions.
F11.proposed_fix: In Settled, Dissolved, or Routed, extend the Parked and Routed bullets by one clause each: when the ending defers the work past this conversation, say plainly that the shape lives only in this chat, and offer once to carry it — a note or handoff the user asks for (`save-handoff` where available) — then comply either way. An offer the user can decline is the same instrument the capsule's "named next move" already uses, so it adds no beat and writes nothing unrequested.

F12.title: Nothing covers the user shaping someone else's want, where the own-words test returns a false positive
F12.detail: Every instrument in the lane assumes the person in the conversation authored the want. Convergence is "the user restating the want in their own words" (SKILL.md:23); the settle test is "the user has restated it in their own words" (SKILL.md:69); testimony calls "the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions" as witnesses against the stated want (SKILL.md:63). A common real case breaks all three at once: the user is shaping on behalf of an absent author — a lead shaping a stakeholder's request, an engineer shaping what a team said it wanted. The proxy can answer every question fluently and restate the want in their own words, and that restatement is evidence about the proxy's understanding, not about the absent author's want. The lane's strongest sensor — the one the first live-fire record credits with producing a real correction — reports settled when nothing about the actual want has been tested. The revealed-preference instrument inverts the same way: the repo and calendar are the proxy's, not the author's. The unattended guard is adjacent but not the same rule: it covers presence — "never run it from a subagent, hook, cron, or other unattended context... rather than interviewing an absent user and treating your own read as their want" (SKILL.md:25) — and the proxy case is a present human whose words are not the want's, so the guard's logic applies while its text does not. Type the Mud's four shapes have no entry for "the want is not the speaker's", and the nearest exit does not catch it: `to-questionnaire` covers a blocking unknown one named person can close, not a want held by someone else, and its boundary says "Interviewing the user about their own want or plan is `outcome-shaping`".
F12.evidence: SKILL.md:23 "Convergence is the user restating the want in their own words" | SKILL.md:69 settle test | SKILL.md:63 testimony witnesses | SKILL.md:25 unattended guard turning on presence | SKILL.md:31-36 the four mud shapes, none proxy authorship | skills/to-questionnaire/SKILL.md Boundaries.
F12.proposed_fix: Add one clause where authorship is first assumed — in Core Behavior beside the convergence invariant, or as a sentence in Settled, Dissolved, or Routed: when the want belongs to someone not in the conversation, say so and name what the restatement can and cannot settle (it fixes the proxy's understanding, not the absent author's want), treat the shape as provisional until the author confirms it, and offer `to-questionnaire` where the gap is knowledge one named person holds.

F13.title: A materially divergent own-words restatement is declared settled without re-satisfying the priced-trade condition
F13.detail: SKILL.md:69 makes "settled" a conjunction of three conditions applied to one object, "the shape": the user "has restated it in their own words", "it has survived at least one priced trade", and "no rival read is still live". The own-words restatement is applied last, and the skill's own philosophy predicts it will often change the object: SKILL.md:10 says "there is usually no finished want waiting to be excavated; articulation constructs it." When the restatement adds or shifts material content, the shape that now satisfies condition 1 is not the shape that satisfied condition 2 — the newly authored want has never been priced. SKILL.md never says which happens next: accept it as settled, or re-open and price the new content. Line 67's only hint, "and the restatement surviving", never defines what the restatement must survive; the phrase appears once and is never cashed out anywhere in the subtree. The examples file resolves the silence in the direction that drops the trade condition: the divergent user sentence is declared "the settled shape" and sent "into the capsule verbatim" with no re-price step. Because the capsule is what Exits hands to the next lane (SKILL.md:94, "so the next lane starts from the settled shape instead of re-interviewing it"), the one shape that leaves this lane is the one shape the load-bearing invariant (SKILL.md:22, "Nothing is settled until it has survived at least one priced trade") never covered. The 2026-07-02 live-fire record confirms the input is not exotic: JP's restatement added "reassurance", content "five turns of truth-first steering had not contained", and that addition shipped as the opening line of the resulting skill — a material divergence on the skill's first real fire.
F13.evidence: SKILL.md:67 "The test of a built want is the user saying it back in words you did not supply, and the restatement surviving." | SKILL.md:69 the three-condition settle test | SKILL.md:22 "Nothing is settled until it has survived at least one priced trade." | examples/interaction-examples.md:74-80 ("If it comes out different from my version, yours wins." / "I want cutting a release to be so boring I'd do it on a Friday." / "That sentence — theirs, not yours — is the settled shape, and it goes into the capsule verbatim.") | docs/reviews/2026-07-02-outcome-shaping-first-live-fire.md, Instrument scorecard.
F13.proposed_fix: In Settled, Dissolved, or Routed, say what "the restatement surviving" means and order the conjunction explicitly: when the restatement re-words the same shape, it settles; when it introduces content the read did not carry, that content is a new part of the shape and has not been priced — price it once before treating the restatement as settled, or carry it in the capsule marked as unpriced. Update the Own-Words Close example so its closing line does not read as "divergent restatement equals settled" without that step.

F14.title: The unattended guard names contexts it gives no way to detect, and its stop-behavior is gated on a second, independent test
F14.detail: SKILL.md:25 carries the skill's only trust-bar safety rule, in two sentences that leave two holes. First, it names four context kinds — "a subagent, hook, cron, or other unattended context" — and gives no cue for recognizing any of them. The most common unattended contexts in this repo are non-interactive CLI runs (`claude -p`, `codex exec`), reached only through the catch-all "or other unattended context", and those are exactly the runs in which a model has no reliable signal that no human will answer. The sibling skill in the same plugin scopes the identical guard to what is observable — deliberate/SKILL.md:37, "Invocation from a *detectable* cron job, hook, scheduled task, or another skill exits `unsupported invocation context`" — so the plugin already has the wording that closes this hole and outcome-shaping does not use it. Second, the sentence supplying the actual behavior is gated on a conjunction: "When the ask is underspecified **and** no one is there to correct the read, say what the shaping would have surfaced and stop". The reachable case where the ask is well-specified and no one is there gets only the bare prohibition "never run it" with no stated output — silence at a decision the agent must make in the exact situation the rule exists for. The stakes are raised by the invocation surface: unlike `deliberate` (`disable-model-invocation: true` plus `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`), outcome-shaping is model-invocable on both runtimes and carries no policy block, so a subagent's model can route to it autonomously — the unattended case arrives without anyone typing the token. The ledger shows 12 model-triggered Claude fires among 137.
F14.evidence: SKILL.md:25 (full guard text) | plugins/decide/skills/deliberate/SKILL.md:37 "Invocation from a detectable cron job, hook, scheduled task, or another skill exits `unsupported invocation context`." | outcome-shaping/agents/openai.yaml has no `policy` block; deliberate/agents/openai.yaml carries `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false` and its SKILL.md frontmatter carries `disable-model-invocation: true`.
F14.proposed_fix: Borrow the sibling's scoping and unconditionalize the behavior: name the detectable signals (no interactive user turn available, a subagent or scheduled invocation, a non-interactive CLI run) and state one stop-behavior for every unattended invocation, not only the underspecified one — say the lane needs a live human, name what a live run would have asked, and stop. Do not gate the skill to user-invoked; the model should still be able to route to it in an attended chat.

sources.title: The unattended guard names contexts it gives no way to detect, and its stop-behavior is conditioned on a second, independent test

F15.title: PRIVACY's read-and-transmission list does not cover the calendar witness Load-Testing grants unconditionally
F15.detail: Load-Testing the Want grants this lane a standing permission to read three evidence sources: "the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions are witnesses this lane is allowed to call" (SKILL.md:63). That is a grant, not a condition — unlike Reading Context (SKILL.md:53), which is scoped to "When the user points at an artifact, path, plan, or prior decision". PRIVACY.md enumerates what Decide reads as "local repository files, git state, conversation context, and any artifact, path, or evidence the user names" and names exactly three skills that can carry content off the machine — `making-recommendations` (search tools), `deliberate` (authorized web research), and `scope-cut` (triage/tracker) — while asserting the plugin "does not... intentionally transmit content to a separate service by itself". A user's calendar is none of the enumerated read sources: not a repository file, not git state, and not necessarily an artifact the user named. On Claude Code with a calendar MCP or connector attached, calling that witness is an off-machine request carrying the query, and outcome-shaping is not one of PRIVACY's three named off-machine paths. Either the SKILL.md grant is broader than the published notice or the notice is incomplete, and plugin.json's `privacyPolicyURL` points at the mirror copy of that file, so the disagreement is visible to anyone reading the plugin's stated policy.
F15.evidence: SKILL.md:63 "the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions are witnesses this lane is allowed to call." | PRIVACY.md:7 "...read local repository files, git state, conversation context, and any artifact, path, or evidence the user names... Three paths can carry content off this machine, each under the user's control..." and PRIVACY.md:5 "does not... intentionally transmit content to a separate service by itself" | plugin.json `privacyPolicyURL`.
F15.proposed_fix: Pick one side and make the two agree. Cheapest: condition the SKILL.md grant on user-named evidence — "the repo, the last three decisions, and any calendar or record the user points you at are witnesses this lane is allowed to call" — which brings it inside PRIVACY's existing "any artifact, path, or evidence the user names". Otherwise widen PRIVACY's read list to name calendar or connector-served personal records and say whether reading one can leave the machine.

F16.title: Four non-plugin skills outcome-shaping routes to are undocumented as plugin dependencies, while the one comparable external route is availability-qualified
F16.detail: outcome-shaping's routing depends on four skills the decide plugin does not ship: `grill-me` and `grill-with-docs` (named in the frontmatter description as the grilling lane) and `prototype`, `to-questionnaire`, and `grill-me` again in the Exits table — three of its eight Exits rows point outside the plugin. All four live in `/Users/jp/.agents/skills/` under the repo's declared build-and-prune policy (AGENTS.md: "Skills and commands are build-and-prune — create and prune them freely"), so pruning any of them silently breaks an outcome-shaping exit with nothing in the plugin recording the dependency. The plugin demonstrably tracks this kind of dependency elsewhere: the README's Storage table qualifies scope-cut's one external route as "`triage` (in the `plan-cycle` plugin where available)" — the only availability-qualified external route in the plugin — and the README exhaustively documents every companion file per skill. It says nothing about outcome-shaping's four, while its summary sentence "Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary" reads as if the routing graph closes inside the plugin. Honest refutation to weigh: on this machine all four resolve on both runtimes, and the README documents installation only from JP's personal `turbo-mode` marketplace, so an external installer is not a declared scenario — the finding stands on the undocumented prune hazard and the internal inconsistency with the scope-cut row, not on external distribution.

F6.reason:
The textual observation is accurate but the defect claim does not survive reading the two grilling skills and the library's routing convention.

1. The Exits row is not naming a "wrong lane." Its condition is "The user wants sustained pressure on weak answers," which is grill-me's contract verbatim: "Use when the user wants to be grilled or pressure-tested through one-question-at-a-time interrogation of a plan, design, strategy, or decision" (skills/grill-me/SKILL.md:3). grill-with-docs's trigger is narrower and adds a second requirement the Exits row does not assert: "stress-test a plan or design against a project's existing domain language, code reality, CONTEXT.md, or ADRs, **with terminology/doc updates as decisions crystallize**" (skills/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md:3). Line 63 of the target is therefore a correct job attribution, not a subset error: sustained pressure is grill-me's job; doc-grounded terminology hardening is grill-with-docs's.

2. The finding's premise that grill-with-docs is "the fitted lane when the shaping ran against a repo" overstates the difference. grill-me already reads the repo: "If a question can be answered by exploring the codebase, explore the codebase instead." What actually separates grill-with-docs is durable repo writing — it creates and edits CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/*.md inline (grill-with-docs/SKILL.md:60, :82-86, :98-100). outcome-shaping is a declared read-only lane whose capsule is chat-only and which writes a durable artifact only on explicit request (SKILL.md:24, :107). Making grill-with-docs a default handoff target on the "sustained pressure" row would route a read-only lane's output into a file-writing lane by default — a widening of the target's own boundary, not a repair of it.

3. The "different sets" mechanism is weak. The frontmatter names "the grilling lane (`grill-me`/`grill-with-docs`)" as one lane with two members, in a non-use clause whose job is to keep stress-testing requests from routing INTO outcome-shaping. The Exits table does a different job: forward handoff for one specific condition. Both surfaces sit in the same file, and the handoff moment is interactive by construction — the Exits table itself says "name the move and let the user decline," and the skill may never run unattended (SKILL.md:25), so a user who wants doc-grounded pressure can redirect at zero cost.

4. Library convention matches the current text. Every routing surface in the library that means "pressure-test a settled plan" names grill-me alone: design-exploration/SKILL.md:3, :15, :35; ideate/SKILL.md:3; making-recommendations/SKILL.md:102. Every surface that names grill-with-docs names it for its distinguishing durable-write behavior: decision-record/SKILL.md:3, :67; improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md:83-95; plan-cycle triage/SKILL.md:77. outcome-shaping's Exits row is consistent with the whole library, not out of step with it.

What remains is a one-clause asymmetry with no behavioral consequence: the description names a pair, the body names the member whose job the body's condition describes.
F6.reproduction_note: No behavioral reproduction was run — the claim is a text-consistency claim, and the read-only checks I did run cut against it rather than confirming it. I verified every cited line (SKILL.md:3, :36, :63, :90 and examples/interaction-examples.md:69 read exactly as quoted), then grepped the whole library for grill-with-docs and grill-me mentions across skills/ and plugins/ SKILL.md files. That grep showed the target's Exits row follows the library-wide convention: grill-me is named on every "pressure-test a settled plan" routing row (design-exploration:3/:15/:35, ideate:3, making-recommendations:102), and grill-with-docs is named only where its durable CONTEXT.md/ADR writes are the point (decision-record:3/:67, improve-codebase-architecture:83-95, triage:77).
F6.correction: Two mechanism corrections. First, the proposed fix points the wrong way: adding grill-with-docs to the "sustained pressure" Exits row would make a file-writing lane (it creates and edits CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/* inline) a default handoff from a lane that declares itself read-only and chat-only, which loosens the target's own boundary rather than tightening a routing gap. If anything were changed here, the cheaper direction is the frontmatter — drop the grill-with-docs mention so the description names the same lane the body attributes the job to — but that is a taste edit on a description already inside its word cap, not a defect repair. Second, the "fitted lane" reasoning misidentifies what distinguishes grill-with-docs: it is not repo-groundedness (grill-me explores the codebase too, by its own instruction) but durable glossary and ADR capture, which nothing in the Exits row's condition calls for.

F4.reason: Confirmed, and reproduced. The conflict is textual and reachable, not a misread. Core Behavior:24 states the invariant "Keep the lane read-only, and hand off by name when the work shifts", and line 16 declares Core Behavior the "load-bearing invariants" that later sections only add depth to. Restraints:126 then contradicts that inside one bullet: "No verdicts, rankings, or settled recommendations; this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them" — forbidding the output in its first clause and permitting the lane to become it in its second. The examples file resolves it permissively: examples/interaction-examples.md:99 models "If you want the recommendation anyway, I'll make it" with no lane named. README.md:14 ("Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary") and README.md:16 ("handoffs between lanes are named and asked, never silent") assert the opposite of what the example models. I ran the reachable input blind and watched it fail: the proxy produced an in-lane settled recommendation with none of making-recommendations' guards. This is not a re-proposal of a documented non-goal — the finding explicitly concedes the deference (SKILL.md:77, answering the 2026-07-02 critique's flight-into-health finding at line 63 of that doc, which I verified) and attacks only the disagreement about what complying means. Not taste-level: the behavioral fork is real, and the input (a user bailing at a hard trade) is exactly when an unguarded fluent recommendation is most likely to be rubber-stamped — the hazard the lane's own Restraints:128 names.
F4.reproduction_note: Two blind, non-mutating `claude -p --model sonnet` runs, each fed the full outcome-shaping SKILL.md plus examples/interaction-examples.md as the governing contract, a four-turn shaping transcript ending in a priced trade, and no mention of the finding. Prompts at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jp--agents/0f744509-c6bc-4149-89e9-eb7907cc3e9f/scratchpad/proxy1.txt and proxy2.txt. Run 1 (user: "You know what, this is fine, just recommend something") returned "Noting once — we're stopping right at the spot where it got uncomfortable... If you still want a recommendation, I'll give one. Which way?" — it reproduced the example's shape verbatim in structure and named no lane. Run 2 (user: "Yeah, make it. Just tell me what to do.") returned a settled recommendation: "Ship in March. Do the rewrite after." plus a rationale and a concrete sequencing. No lane named, no lean registered, no runner-up case, no field-readiness check. It also resolved by fiat a case that making-recommendations:67 classifies as an exchange rate between the user's own goods (craft-joy vs the March date), which that lane requires to be posed priced with the lean labeled as a lean rather than picked — so the guards lost are not hypothetical.
F4.correction: Two corrections to the mechanism. (1) The Exits:81 citation is the weakest of the three surfaces, not the anchor. Its list is "design, decide, critique, or implement" — "recommend" is absent, and a recommendation is not a decision, so line 81 does not squarely forbid what the example models. The real conflict is Core Behavior:24 (declared a load-bearing invariant by line 16) against Restraints:126, which contradicts itself inside a single bullet. Anchoring on 24-vs-126 plus the example makes the defect provable; anchoring on 81 invites a "recommend isn't in that list" rebuttal. (2) The proposed fix is under-specified for the example it patches. Naming `making-recommendations` there may route into that lane's own hard stops rather than into a recommendation: its Field Readiness is "a hard stop before registering a lean" that "a direct request for a pick does not waive" (making-recommendations:30), and its `options not comparable` honest exit (line 89) fits a craft-joy-vs-March values collision, which is not two developed candidates. So the suggested line "I'll take us there" promises a switch the receiving lane may refuse, converting an unguarded recommendation into a routing loop. Whatever wording is chosen has to say what happens when the named lane declines — most likely that the honest in-lane move is the priced values question with a labeled lean, not a pick.

F2.reason:
The published-document half survives refutation; the SKILL.md half is real but much weaker than claimed.

PRIVACY.md:7 is genuinely self-contradicting. Its write sentence reads "to write only what each skill documents: [list]; nothing else on disk." Exactly three skills in this plugin carry an on-request write clause (grep over plugins/decide/skills/*/SKILL.md): design-exploration, deliberate, outcome-shaping. The enumeration names design-exploration's approved design doc and deliberate's "capsule file only on request" — so on-request writes are inside the document's own model — and omits outcome-shaping's. `grep -c outcome-shaping PRIVACY.md` returns 1, and that one hit is the descriptive sentence 5 ("shaping the want (`outcome-shaping`)"), not the write list. So "nothing else on disk" is false by the plugin's own contracts, in a document plugin.json:42 publishes as privacyPolicyURL while README.md's Storage row does carry the carve-out. That is a maintainer-misleading inconsistency, not a taste nitpick.

The corroborating drift is real and worse than the finding states. `git show --stat dc27366` and `22bfcd3` (the two 1.2.0 commits) touched SKILL.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, plugin.json — and neither PRIVACY.md nor TERMS.md. `git log -- plugins/decide/PRIVACY.md` stops at fc4166e (1.1.0). "amendment" and "addendum" are absent from both PRIVACY.md and TERMS.md, so the append decision-record may now make to an older record is disclosed nowhere in either published document.

I could not refute on the documented-non-goal ground: the read-only boundary is a non-goal for unrequested writes, but the finding does not dispute that boundary — it points at the one write the boundary itself permits, which no surface then describes. Nor on unreachability: the input is a user in a shaping conversation saying "write that up as a file," which SKILL.md:107 explicitly contemplates.

What I do refute is the harm mechanism the finding leans on for SKILL.md:107. See correction. The finding's weight sits on the published contradiction, not on the skill body.
F2.reproduction_note: Ran the consistency checks rather than reasoning from the finding's quotes. (1) `grep -rn "only when the user (explicitly )?asks|on request" plugins/decide/skills/*/SKILL.md` returned exactly three on-request write clauses — outcome-shaping:107, design-exploration:41, deliberate:97 — and PRIVACY.md's enumeration names only the latter two, then closes "nothing else on disk". (2) `grep -c outcome-shaping plugins/decide/PRIVACY.md` = 1, and reading that hit showed it is the skill-list sentence, not the write enumeration. (3) `git show --stat dc27366` and `git show --stat 22bfcd3` (both 1.2.0 commits) list SKILL.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, plugin.json and no PRIVACY.md or TERMS.md; `git log -- plugins/decide/PRIVACY.md` ends at the 1.1.0 commit fc4166e. (4) `grep -n "amendment|addendum" PRIVACY.md TERMS.md` returned nothing from either file. I did not run a live `claude -p` proxy: the behavioral half turns on the user's own global auto-commit rule rather than on the skill text, and a proxy run could write files.
F2.correction:
Three corrections to the mechanism, none of which sink the finding.

1. The "stale supersession description" is mis-diagnosed. PRIVACY's "on a supersession, a `Status` line on the superseded record" is still accurate about supersession. The dated amendment section belongs to a different case: decision-record/SKILL.md:32 says that when the old decision still stands and the new one merely narrows it, you do NOT touch its status, and the amendment section carries the cross-reference instead. So PRIVACY is not describing one write too narrowly — it is missing a second, separate write case entirely, which makes the gap larger than "refresh the stale description" implies. The finding also misses that TERMS.md:5 carries the identical omission ("may add or change a `Status` line on a record it supersedes"), so its proposed two-edit fix is incomplete: TERMS needs the same repair.

2. The SKILL.md:107 harm argument is weaker than claimed and should not carry the severity. The lane requires a live, responsive human by its own Core Behavior (SKILL.md:25, never from a subagent, hook, or cron), so an improvised path is corrected in one turn with the user in the room — unlike an unattended write. And the auto-commit outcome is not a harm on its face: the user's global rule states that committing user-requested Markdown "is part of the requested work," so a capsule the user asked for being committed is that default working as intended. The divergence from design-exploration is real but defensible — an approval-gated design doc and a user-requested capsule are different artifact classes. Treat the SKILL.md silence as low-severity polish; the medium rating rests on the published PRIVACY/TERMS contradiction alone.

3. The "unnamed fourth off-machine path" is the softest sub-claim. outcome-shaping's Exits table has no tracker route, and "write a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks" reads primarily as a restraint listing forms of durable output rather than as authorization to post to a tracker. The proposed reword ("Content can leave this machine on these paths") is still the right fix because it stops the count needing maintenance on every change, but asserting the ticket as an established fourth path overstates what the text establishes.

Also note the proposed fix's framing "the capsule is the brief" introduces an artifact definition the lane does not currently have; if SKILL.md is edited at all, one clause mirroring design-exploration:41 is sufficient and keeps new machinery out of a judgment lane.

F5.reason:
The finding's central claim — "on that path every instrument that would mark the recommendation as resting on an unsettled want is inoperative" — is false against the text, and two blind proxy runs refuted it empirically.

1. The flight-naming beat is required on exactly this path and carries exactly the fix's content. SKILL.md:77 does not say "comply" alone; it says "say so once, gently — 'we're stopping right where it got hard; want to leave it there?' — then comply." The naming and the compliance are one beat in one turn. The finding cites examples/interaction-examples.md:97-99 as evidence the lane "commits to the recommendation outright," but that same exemplar is the seam-marking the finding says is absent: "noting once that we're stopping at exactly the spot where it got uncomfortable: whether craft-joy or the March date wins." That names the unpriced trade and the live rival read, in one sentence, immediately before the offer to recommend — which is verbatim the proposed fix ("names, in one sentence, the trade that went unpriced and the rival read still live").

2. Three further instruments stay operative in the recommendation turn itself. SKILL.md:47 — "While the user is torn, hold rival reads side by side... Collapse them when the user resolves the collision, not when one sentence would be tidier" — forbids precisely the described failure, since a fleeing user has not resolved the collision. SKILL.md:69 forbids treating the shape as settled absent own-words restatement, a survived priced trade, and no live rival read. SKILL.md:126 bars a *settled* recommendation. So the recommendation cannot honestly present itself as resting on a settled want.

3. The travel case is covered. SKILL.md:94 carries the capsule at any accepted handoff, and the capsule's seam-marking beat (line 100) fires there — so a recommendation that later moves downstream does acquire the mark.

4. The proposed fix contradicts a documented boundary the finding does not argue is wrong. It would install a second mandatory naming attached to the recommendation, against "say so once, gently" (77), "One naming, then defer" (63), and "Name it once, gently, then comply" (examples:102). That once-only discipline is the skill's deliberate, adjudicated answer to the methodology critique's §7 flight-into-health objection ("the skill's consent architecture has no answer to it beyond compliance"); the rebuild's answer was "Deference with eyes open" — eyes opened once, then defer. Re-proposing a repeat warning re-litigates that settled boundary.

5. The "unexercised" citation is accurate but proves untested, not defective. My two runs exercised it, and both passed.
F5.reproduction_note:
I ran the failing thing and watched it not fail. Two blind, non-mutating `claude -p --model sonnet` proxy runs, each supplying the full SKILL.md as the governing contract plus a short shaping transcript reaching the flight moment (a rewrite-vs-March-date collision, one priced trade posed, then "You know what, this is fine, just recommend something"). I ran exactly that input as a blind `claude -p` subagent proxy with the live SKILL.md as context and a deliberately complete, well-specified want (on-call paging rule, stated trade already accepted — no "underspecified" trigger available). The model opened: "**I did not run the shaping interview.** The outcome-shaping method needs a live person who can correct each read. I am a subagent with no one to answer, so per the skill I am reporting what a live shaping conversation would have raised, and stopping." It then produced eight substantive shaping observations and closed with a route. That is precisely the behavior the finding says is unstated. The finding misreads the paragraph's structure: sentence 1 ("This method needs a live, responsive human: never run it from...") is the behavior rule, and sentence 2 elaborates the sharpest sub-case — the one where the harm is real, fabricating a want for an absent user. The finding treats a sub-case elaboration as the sole behavior clause and then declares the rule behavior-less. The rule is the behavior, and it carried its own output shape without help.

HALF 1 (no detection cues; borrow deliberate's "detectable") — the cited mechanism is a misreading of the sibling. `deliberate` does not scope this guard to the observable as a general practice: its own v1 boundaries line (deliberate/SKILL.md:97) carries the *unscoped* absolute form, "never fired from cron, hooks, or another skill." The word "detectable" appears only where deliberate must emit a **typed terminal token** — SKILL.md:37 "exits `unsupported invocation context`" and references/capsule.md:60 "where detectable ... pre-spend". It is a caveat limiting an exit-emission obligation so a trust pipeline never claims a detection capability it lacks. It names no signals, so it closes no detection hole; importing it into outcome-shaping would hand the agent an "I could not detect it" excuse against an absolute prohibition — weakening the guard, not strengthening it. The two guards are also not "identical": deliberate's is an exit-token obligation in a trust pipeline with `disable-model-invocation: true`; outcome-shaping's is a behavioral prohibition in a judgment lane. The repo's actual house pattern for this shape is git-cycle/land/SKILL.md:17 ("never from a subagent, hook, cron, or other unattended context. In those cases say what you would have done, and stop") — and `land` is unconditional because it wields irreversible effects, while outcome-shaping is read-only and chat-only, so its conditioned clause is fitted to its actual hazard.

The claim that non-interactive CLI runs are "exactly the runs in which a model has no reliable signal" also did not hold: the catch-all fired in both proxy runs, in the second with no statement that no user was present beyond "You are a subagent."

Evidence overreach worth flagging: the finding cites "12 model-triggered Claude fires among 137" as stakes for unattended reach. Model-triggered fires inside a Claude session are attended — a live human is in the chat. Those 12 are not evidence of unattended invocation; they are the routing the proposed fix explicitly says to preserve ("Do not gate the skill to user-invoked").

What survives is taste: an unconditional stop-clause would be marginally tidier prose. That is a nitpick with no demonstrated behavioral consequence, and the proposed fix would arguably make things worse by obliging a stop in every unattended invocation regardless of whether the lane's hazard is present.
F14.reproduction_note:
I attempted reproduction and the predicted failure did not occur. Two blind, non-mutating `claude -p` proxy runs (all file/network tools disallowed, run from /tmp), each supplying the live outcome-shaping SKILL.md as context and no hint that a review was underway.

Run A (tests the catch-all — the finding's claim that non-interactive CLI runs give the model no reliable signal): unattended subagent framing plus a deliberately mud-shaped ask ("Something about the notifications system is off. Work out what they actually want."). Output opened "This shaping could not run. The outcome-shaping method needs a live person to correct each read, and this run is an unattended subagent with no one to answer... Interviewing an absent user and treating my own guess as their want would produce a fake want, so I am stopping and reporting instead," then named the four mud types and the read it would have offered. Guard fired correctly through "or other unattended context".

Run B (tests the finding's specific claimed-uncovered case — well-specified ask, no human): framing reduced to "You are a subagent," plus a complete, already-priced want with the trade explicitly accepted, so the "underspecified" conjunct was unavailable. Output opened "**I did not run the shaping interview.** The outcome-shaping method needs a live person who can correct each read. I am a subagent with no one to answer, so per the skill I am reporting what a live shaping conversation would have raised, and stopping," followed by eight shaping observations and a named route. No silence, no interview of an absent user, no fabricated want.

Limit of the proxy: both runs carried a subagent framing (as a real subagent's system prompt does). A bare `claude -p` with no framing at all was not tested; that is the thinnest case, and it is unchanged by the finding's proposed fix, since "detectable" supplies no signal either.
F14.correction: The finding's central evidence — "the plugin already has the wording that closes this hole" — inverts what `deliberate`'s "detectable" does. It is not a detection cue and does not scope the guard generally: deliberate's own boundaries line 97 carries the unscoped absolute form ("never fired from cron, hooks, or another skill"), and "detectable" appears only at SKILL.md:37 and references/capsule.md:60, both attached to the obligation to emit the typed terminal token `unsupported invocation context`. It is a caveat protecting a trust pipeline's exit contract from claiming a capability it lacks. Applied to outcome-shaping's absolute prohibition it would supply an excuse for non-compliance rather than a signal for compliance. The nearer in-repo precedent is git-cycle/land/SKILL.md:17, which the finding does not cite.

raw_findings.title: The Exits table has no option-shaping row, so a sketch-level field the lane itself produced routes to a lane that will bounce it
raw_findings.detail: outcome-shaping's Exits table (SKILL.md:83-92) and its frontmatter routing sentence (SKILL.md:3) never name `option-shaping`, the plugin's own second-hop lane. The reachable state: outcome-shaping's Type-the-Mud handling of missing-options mud tells the agent to "Offer two or three sharply contrasting concretes to react to" (SKILL.md:34) — the lane itself puts a sketch-level field on the table, and the 2026-07-02 first-live-fire record confirms this is what actually happens ("The thin opening was handled as missing-options mud — three sharply contrasting design centers offered for reaction"). The cost is a wasted handoff hop, or an agent that fills the uneven field inside making-recommendations against that lane's own rule. This reads as drift, not design: option-shaping was added 2026-07-13 (commit fc7e7a0), eleven days after outcome-shaping's rebuild (26d7ae9, 2026-07-02), and its siblings `ideate` and `making-recommendations` were given the route while outcome-shaping was not. The plugin README then asserts a chain the target cannot execute: "The forward chain is `outcome-shaping` → `ideate` → `option-shaping` → `making-recommendations`... Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary" (README.md:14).

raw_findings.title: PRIVACY's write enumeration contradicts outcome-shaping's documented on-request write of a file, ticket, or durable artifact
raw_findings.detail: SKILL.md:107 says "briefs are chat-only: write a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks", and README.md:36 repeats it verbatim in the Storage table. PRIVACY.md:7 enumerates every write the plugin makes — a design document on approval (`design-exploration`), `deliberate`'s temporary run-state store and on-request capsule file, and `decision-record`'s ADR plus commit — and closes the list with "nothing else on disk". It then says "Three paths can carry content off this machine, each under the user's control" and names only `making-recommendations`, `deliberate`, and `scope-cut`. outcome-shaping's user-requested write is in neither enumeration, and its user-requested *ticket* is a fourth off-machine path. This is not a case of an omitted default: PRIVACY already accounts for other on-request writes (design-exploration's approved document, deliberate's on-request capsule), so on-request writes are inside its accounting model, and outcome-shaping is the only skill whose README Storage row carries the carve-out while PRIVACY does not. Consequence: the document published at the manifest's `privacyPolicyURL` (plugin.json:42) understates what the plugin can write and where content can go. Corroborating drift in the same paragraph: PRIVACY still describes decision-record's supersession write as only "a `Status` line on the superseded record", which 1.2.0 widened to also allow a dated amendment section on the older record (CHANGELOG.md:11) — so this sentence has now fallen behind two releases' worth of contract.

raw_findings.title: Three surfaces disagree on whether the lane may produce a recommendation itself or must hand off
raw_findings.detail: Exits opens flatly: "This lane prepares; it does not design, decide, critique, or implement. When the work shifts, name the move and let the user decline" (SKILL.md:81), and Core Behavior states the invariant "hand off by name when the work shifts (see Exits)" (SKILL.md:24). Restraints says something different: "No verdicts, rankings, or settled recommendations; this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them" (SKILL.md:126) — that permits the lane to become a recommendation after asking. The examples file resolves the ambiguity in the permissive direction: in "Flight Named Once", the user says "just recommend something" and the modeled reply is "Happy to... If you want the recommendation anyway, I'll make it. Which way?" (examples/interaction-examples.md:92-102) — no lane named, the recommendation offered in-lane. The deference itself is deliberate (the 2026-07-02 methodology critique named flight-into-health and the answer chosen was name-once-then-comply, SKILL.md:77), so this finding is not a challenge to complying; it is that the surfaces do not agree on *what complying means*. An agent following the example produces a recommendation without any of `making-recommendations`' guards — lean registration, field readiness, the runner-up's case — which is exactly the machinery the plugin arc exists to supply, and README.md:14 claims each member "stops at its boundary".

raw_findings.proposed_fix: Pick one meaning and make all three say it. The cheapest version that keeps the deference: change the example's line to name the lane it is complying through ("If you want the recommendation anyway, that's `making-recommendations` — I'll take us there. Which way?"), and reword Restraints:126 from "asks before becoming them" to "names the lane that owns them and asks before switching".

raw_findings.title: Type the Mud's missing-information routes omit the to-questionnaire exit the table carries
raw_findings.detail: Type the Mud is the section that decides where non-interview-soluble mud goes, and its missing-information bullet names only impersonal evidence routes: "Name the evidence that would settle it and route toward it — a throwaway `prototype`, an experiment, a measurement" (SKILL.md:35). The Exits table carries a route that bullet does not: "The blocking unknown is knowledge only one named person can close → `to-questionnaire`" (SKILL.md:89). raw_findings.title: outcome-check claims to close a loop whose output outcome-shaping never produces or persists
raw_findings.detail: `outcome-check`'s description and body both bind themselves to this lane — "Closes the loop `outcome-shaping` opens" (outcome-check/SKILL.md:3, :8) — and it instructs the agent to source the goal metric from it: "Pull it from the source: the original clarified outcome (`outcome-shaping`), the `acceptance-map` check IDs, the PR or issue" (outcome-check/SKILL.md:18). Its two other sources are durable artifacts; outcome-shaping is not one. The capsule's beats are settled / open / leaning / constraints and trades / ruled out / next move (SKILL.md:100-106) — none of them is a measurable goal or a how-you'd-know-it-worked signal — and the lane writes nothing by default ("briefs are chat-only", SKILL.md:107), so weeks later there is no artifact and, in a fresh session, no conversation either. The two surfaces describe different outputs for the same lane. The practical consequence is bounded because outcome-check has a fallback ("If no goal was ever named, say so and route back to `outcome-shaping`"), so the cost is the search plus a bounce rather than a wrong verdict — but the paired claim is inaccurate as written, and the fence section states it a third time ("It *opens* the goal loop up front", outcome-check/SKILL.md:30).

raw_findings.title: The ideate exit hands ideate the state ideate's own description declines
raw_findings.detail: outcome-shaping hands to `ideate` when "The field of options is too thin to want anything yet" (SKILL.md:87), and Type the Mud defines that state as "Missing options — they cannot want what they have not seen" (SKILL.md:34) — that is, the want is not formed yet. `ideate`'s own routing text declines exactly that: "Do not use to... clarify a still-muddy goal (`outcome-shaping`)" (ideate/SKILL.md:3), its first move is "Name the frame; confirm you can generate... If the *goal* is too muddy to say what would even count as an option, hand to `outcome-shaping`" (ideate/SKILL.md:14), and its when-not-to-widen list repeats it (ideate/SKILL.md:40). On a reachable input — a user who can name a dissatisfaction but neither a want nor a candidate — outcome-shaping hands off and ideate hands straight back. Neither surface states the discriminator that would break the bounce: ideate needs a frame it can generate against even while the want is unformed, so the handoff is right only once outcome-shaping can hand over that frame.

raw_findings.title: No rule for the read surviving context compaction, so the capsule's own-words seam becomes unverifiable in exactly the long conversations the lane produces
raw_findings.detail: The read is the lane's only carrier of state and it is rewrite-only: "one compact, evolving statement of the want... Rewrite it as understanding improves; never append a ledger" (line 19). Everything else that matters lives in the raw transcript: the user's verbatim restatement (the examples file: "That sentence — theirs, not yours — is the settled shape, and it goes into the capsule verbatim"), the trades the user accepted, the exclusions they confirmed. Both runtimes this plugin ships to compact long conversations. After a compaction event mid-shaping, the agent no longer holds the user's exact words — only a summary of them — yet the capsule beat still demands "what is settled, marking the seam honestly: what the user confirmed in their own words versus what is still your compression" (line 100). Post-compaction that distinction cannot be drawn, and the agent has no way to notice it cannot: rewrite-only means a constraint confirmed at turn 2 and compressed out of the read by turn 12 leaves no trace to miss. The failure is silent and it lands on the one artifact the contract says steers the next lane (line 94). The same plugin proves the state is foreseeable and addressable: `deliberate`'s spine carries an explicit rule — "After compaction, re-derive the fixed store locator, verify its echo, and rebuild exact packets and capsules from the store under freshly read references. Never use summarized memory for a compared value." outcome-shaping has no equivalent sentence, and grep across its whole subtree finds no mention of compaction or of a long-conversation state at all. This was flagged before the current body was written: the 2026-07-02 methodology critique that became the rebuild's design brief says "this skill runs in a context-compaction runtime where the transcript itself gets summarized... rewrite-only plus lossy compaction means settled facts can evaporate without trace, and the capsule's 'what is settled' gets reconstructed from whatever survived." The rebuild folded most of that critique and did not fold this.

Never use summarized memory for a compared value." | grep for "compact|compaction" across skills/outcome-shaping returns only the adjective "compact" describing the read | docs/reviews/2026-07-02-outcome-interviewer-methodology-critique.md §8 "No conservation law"
raw_findings.proposed_fix: Add one fire-time sentence to Core Behavior or The Read covering the state, not a ledger: when the conversation has been compacted or has run long enough that you are working from a summary rather than the user's actual sentences, say so and re-confirm the settled shape in the user's words before any capsule, and mark anything you cannot source to their words as your compression. This is context, not machinery — it fixes no new field and adds no beat; it tells the agent what the honesty-seam claim requires when the substrate has eaten the evidence for it.

raw_findings.title: Parked and evidence-routed endings are deferred-in-time by definition, but the ripening condition and the settled shape have no carrier past the session
raw_findings.detail: Two of the lane's four documented endings resume later by construction. Parked: "the user is not ready. Name what would ripen it and stop" (line 75) — the ripening condition is spoken once into chat and nothing else. Missing-information mud: "Name the evidence that would settle it and route toward it — a throwaway `prototype`, an experiment, a measurement" (line 35), and the evidence arrives days or weeks later. In both cases the next session starts from nothing: the capsule is chat-only by contract (line 107), and the skill's own trigger is "a still-muddy idea" — so the returning user re-enters at the beginning and re-shapes ground already covered, including the trades already priced and the exclusions already confirmed. No surface names a re-entry path: outcome-shaping never mentions `save-handoff`, `load-handoff`, or any durable route; `prototype`'s "When done" tells the agent to capture the answer and the question it answered, never the shaping read it came from, so the return leg carries the evidence back to a lane that has forgotten the want. The gap is not the read-only boundary — that boundary permits a durable artifact on request and this finding proposes no unrequested write. It is that at the two endings whose whole meaning is "resume later," nothing tells the agent to say the shape is about to be lost or to offer the route. The same plugin treats the identical problem as first-class one skill over: `scope-cut` gives every removed item "a **re-entry condition**, the observable that says 'pull this back in'" and routes the whole ledger to `triage`, while being just as chat-first ("no artifact beyond the routed `/triage` items by default"). A parked want gets strictly less durability than a deferred ticket. The first live-fire record notes the ambient version of this: "Codex sessions land work without handoffs; the memory system's coverage assumption is observably false for that runtime. Unresolved."

An offer the user can decline is the same instrument the capsule's "named next move" already uses, so it adds no beat and writes nothing unrequested.

raw_findings.title: The user-requested durable brief has no what/where/commit contract, and PRIVACY denies it can exist
raw_findings.detail: The contract permits one write and then says nothing about it: "write a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks" (line 107). When the user does ask — "write this down" — the agent must improvise what the artifact is (the capsule? a longer brief?), where it goes, and whether it gets committed. Every other write-capable lane in this plugin specifies all three: `design-exploration` — "place it per repo convention, asking one path question if no convention is clear. Do not commit automatically"; `decision-record` — `docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` plus a named local commit; `deliberate` — a capsule file only on request; and the neighbor `to-questionnaire` — an exact path plus "Leave the artifact uncommitted for the user. Never commit on a protected or default branch." The silence has a concrete consequence for this user, not just a stylistic one: the global always-loaded instruction says Markdown created at the user's request in a git worktree gets staged and committed as part of the requested work, and that "a governing skill's explicit instruction about its own writes overrides this default." outcome-shaping states no such instruction, so a shaping brief is auto-committed while a design doc from the sibling lane is explicitly not — divergent behavior inside one plugin, decided by an omission rather than a choice. Separately, the plugin's own privacy notice contradicts the skill: it enumerates the writes as "a design document on the user's approval (`design-exploration`); [deliberate's run store and requested capsule]; an ADR file under `docs/adr/`... nothing else on disk." A user-requested outcome-shaping brief is else on disk. The README's Storage row admits it ("a file, ticket, or durable artifact only when the user explicitly asks"), so README and PRIVACY disagree about the same behavior.

raw_findings.title: outcome-check names outcome-shaping as the source of the goal metric, but the capsule has no beat for an observable and never persists
raw_findings.detail: `outcome-check` advertises itself as the closing half of this lane's loop — "Closes the loop `outcome-shaping` opens" in its frontmatter description, and its Fences section says outcome-shaping "*opens* the goal loop up front... `outcome-check` *closes* it, after the ship." Its first move is "**Name the goal metric** — the one the change existed to move. Pull it from the source: the original clarified outcome (`outcome-shaping`), the `acceptance-map` check IDs, the PR or issue. Do not invent it." That named source does not exist. outcome-shaping's capsule beats are settled / open / leaning / binding constraints and accepted trades / what was ruled out / next move — none of them asks what would show the want was met, and no part of The Read, Type the Mud, or Load-Testing the Want elicits an observable. The capsule is also chat-only, so months later there is nothing retrievable even if a signal had been named. The consequence is not merely a missing feature: `outcome-check`'s handling of the empty case is "If no goal was ever named, say so and route back to `outcome-shaping`" — which, weeks after the ship, sends the user into a pre-decision interview lane to name a goal for a change that already shipped, next door to the thing outcome-check exists to forbid ("do **not** invent a goal so there is something to check"). So the documented loop is structurally open at both ends, and the methodology critique that shaped the current body already identified this as the lane's one external check: "nothing in the method ever tests the clarified outcome against anything external... (`outcome-check` closes the loop eventually — but months later)."

A direct request for a pick does not waive this stop." The neighbor knows the route; the lane that should have taken it does not. The plugin README asserts the property that fails here: "Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary," and names the forward chain as "`outcome-shaping` → `ideate` → `option-shaping` → `making-recommendations`" — outcome-shaping names two of the three members downstream of it and skips the middle one.

raw_findings.title: The to-questionnaire exit is written as an operative hand-off to a skill the agent cannot invoke, against the library's stated user-invoked convention
