raw_findings.title: Nothing covers the user shaping someone else's want, where the own-words test returns a false positive
raw_findings.detail: Every instrument in the lane assumes the person in the conversation is the author of the want. Convergence is "the user restating the want in their own words" (line 23); the settle test is "the user has restated it in their own words" (line 69); testimony calls "the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions" as witnesses against "the stated want" (line 63). A common real case breaks all three at once: the user is shaping on behalf of an absent author — a lead shaping a stakeholder's request, an engineer shaping what a team said it wanted. The proxy can answer every question fluently and restate the want in their own words, and that restatement is evidence about the proxy's understanding, not about the absent author's want. The lane's strongest sensor — the one the first live-fire record credits with producing a real correction — reports settled when nothing about the actual want has been tested. The revealed-preference instrument inverts the same way: the repo and calendar are the proxy's, not the author's. The unattended guard is close to this but not the same rule: it covers presence — "never run it from a subagent, hook, cron, or other unattended context... rather than interviewing an absent user and treating your own read as their want" (line 25). The proxy case is a present human whose words are not the want's, so the guard's logic applies while its text does not. Type the Mud's four shapes (missing words, missing options, missing information, colliding wants) also have no entry for "the want is not the speaker's," and the nearest exits do not catch it: `to-questionnaire` covers a blocking unknown one named person can close, not a want held by someone else, and its own boundary says "Interviewing the user about their own want or plan is `outcome-shaping`" — describing the case this lane actually handles rather than flagging the proxy case as excluded.

raw_findings.proposed_fix: Add one clause where authorship is first assumed — in Core Behavior beside the convergence invariant, or as a sentence in Settled, Dissolved, or Routed: when the want belongs to someone not in the conversation, say so and name what the restatement can and cannot settle — it fixes the proxy's understanding, not the absent author's want — and treat the shape as provisional until the author confirms it, offering `to-questionnaire` where the gap is knowledge one named person holds. That is context that keeps the sensor honest, not a new beat or field.

raw_findings.title: A materially divergent own-words restatement is declared settled without re-satisfying the priced-trade condition
raw_findings.detail: SKILL.md line 69 makes "settled" a conjunction of three conditions applied to one object, "the shape": the user "has restated it in their own words", "it has survived at least one priced trade", and "no rival read is still live". The own-words restatement is the last condition applied, and the skill's own philosophy predicts it will often change the object: line 10 says "there is usually no finished want waiting to be excavated; articulation constructs it." When the restatement adds or shifts material content, the shape that now satisfies condition 1 is not the shape that satisfied condition 2 — the newly authored want has never been priced. SKILL.md never says which happens next: accept it as settled, or re-open and price the new content. Line 67's only hint, "and the restatement surviving", never defines what the restatement must survive; the phrase appears once and is never cashed out anywhere in the subtree. The examples file resolves the silence in the direction that drops the trade condition: the divergent user sentence is declared "the settled shape" and sent "into the capsule verbatim" with no re-price step. Because the capsule is what the Exits section hands to the next lane (line 94, "so the next lane starts from the settled shape instead of re-interviewing it"), the one shape that leaves this lane is the one shape the skill's own load-bearing invariant (line 22, "Nothing is settled until it has survived at least one priced trade") never covered. The 2026-07-02 live-fire record confirms this input is not exotic: JP's restatement added "reassurance", content "five turns of truth-first steering had not contained", and that addition shipped as the opening line of the resulting skill — a material divergence, on the skill's first real fire.

If it comes out different from my version, yours wins." / User: "I want cutting a release to be so boring I'd do it on a Friday." / "That sentence — theirs, not yours — is the settled shape, and it goes into the capsule verbatim." docs/reviews/2026-07-02-outcome-shaping-first-live-fire.md, Instrument scorecard: "JP's restatement ... added 'reassurance', which five turns of truth-first steering had not contained."

Update the Own-Words Close example so its closing line does not read as "divergent restatement equals settled" without that step.

raw_findings.title: The unattended guard names contexts it gives no way to detect, and its stop-behavior is conditioned on a second, independent test
raw_findings.detail: Line 25 carries the skill's only trust-bar safety rule, in two sentences that leave two holes. First, it names four context kinds — "a subagent, hook, cron, or other unattended context" — and gives no cue for recognizing any of them. The most common unattended contexts in this repo are non-interactive CLI runs (`claude -p`, `codex exec`), reached only through the catch-all "or other unattended context", and those are exactly the runs in which a model has no reliable signal that no human will answer. The sibling skill in the same plugin scopes the identical guard to what is observable — deliberate/SKILL.md:37, "Invocation from a *detectable* cron job, hook, scheduled task, or another skill exits `unsupported invocation context`" — so the plugin already has the wording that closes this hole, and outcome-shaping does not use it. Second, the sentence that supplies the actual behavior is gated on a conjunction: "When the ask is underspecified **and** no one is there to correct the read, say what the shaping would have surfaced and stop". The reachable case where the ask is well-specified and no one is there gets only the bare prohibition "never run it" with no stated output — silence at a decision the agent must make in the exact situation the rule exists for. The stakes are raised by the invocation surface: unlike deliberate (`disable-model-invocation: true` plus `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false`), outcome-shaping is model-invocable on both runtimes and carries no policy block, so a subagent's model can route to it autonomously — the unattended case arrives without anyone typing the token. The ledger already shows 12 model-triggered Claude fires among 137.

When the ask is underspecified and no one is there to correct the read, say what the shaping would have surfaced and stop — report the underspecification rather than interviewing an absent user and treating your own read as their want." /Users/jp/.agents/plugins/decide/skills/deliberate/SKILL.md:37 "Invocation from a detectable cron job, hook, scheduled task, or another skill exits `unsupported invocation context`." outcome-shaping/agents/openai.yaml has no `policy` block; deliberate/agents/openai.yaml carries `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false` and deliberate/SKILL.md frontmatter carries `disable-model-invocation: true`.

Do not gate the skill to user-invoked; the model should still be able to route to it in an attended chat.

raw_findings.title: Complying with a flight-into-recommendation produces an in-lane recommendation with no seam-marking, because the capsule only fires at handoffs
raw_findings.detail: The user fleeing an uncomfortable trade and saying "just recommend something" is a documented, deliberately-accepted input: line 77 says name it once, gently, "then comply with whatever they choose. Deference with eyes open." That boundary is not what I am challenging. The gap is what "comply" covers. Restraints line 126 permits an in-lane recommendation — "No verdicts, rankings, or settled recommendations; this lane prepares those moves and asks before becoming them" — and the examples file commits to it outright ("If you want the recommendation anyway, I'll make it"). The Exits row that would route this instead requires "Criteria and two or more serious options are clear enough to compare", which is precisely what is not true at the flight moment, so the in-lane path is the reachable one. On that path every instrument that would mark the recommendation as resting on an unsettled want is inoperative: the capsule — the only place the skill requires marking "what the user confirmed in their own words versus what is still your compression" — fires only "at a handoff point, or when the user asks to summarize" (line 98), and an in-lane recommendation is neither. So the agent produces a recommendation built on a want that failed the priced trade, with rival reads still live, and nothing in the text requires it to say so. That is the skill's own named hazard ("a crisp wrong read is more convincing than a true muddy one") realized at the moment the skill identifies as the most dangerous. The 2026-07-02 live-fire record notes this instrument is still unexercised: "Flight-named-once / evidence testimony — unexercised."

raw_findings.title: PRIVACY.md's access and transmission list does not cover the calendar witness Load-Testing grants unconditionally
raw_findings.detail: SKILL.md's Load-Testing the Want grants this lane a standing permission to read three evidence sources: "the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions are witnesses this lane is allowed to call." That is a grant, not a condition -- unlike Reading Context (line 53), which is scoped to "When the user points at an artifact, path, plan, or prior decision". PRIVACY.md enumerates what Decide reads as "local repository files, git state, conversation context, and any artifact, path, or evidence the user names" and then names exactly three skills that can carry content off the machine -- `making-recommendations` (search tools), `deliberate` (authorized web research), and `scope-cut` (triage/tracker) -- asserting the plugin "does not... intentionally transmit content to a separate service by itself". A user's calendar is none of the enumerated read sources: it is not a repository file, not git state, and not necessarily an artifact the user named. On Claude Code with a calendar MCP or connector attached, calling that witness is an off-machine request carrying the query, and outcome-shaping is not one of PRIVACY's three named off-machine paths. Either the SKILL.md grant is broader than the published privacy notice, or the notice is incomplete. PRIVACY.md is a published surface: plugin.json's `privacyPolicyURL` points at the mirror copy of this file, so the disagreement is visible to anyone reading the plugin's stated policy.
raw_findings.evidence: SKILL.md:63 "Where artifacts can testify, let them. Stated and revealed wants diverge, and the repo, the calendar, and the last three decisions are witnesses this lane is allowed to call." PRIVACY.md: "Decide requests may cause the runtime to read local repository files, git state, conversation context, and any artifact, path, or evidence the user names... Three paths can carry content off this machine, each under the user's control: `making-recommendations`... `deliberate`... and `scope-cut`..." and "It does not create background files, register hooks, run services, or intentionally transmit content to a separate service by itself." plugin.json: `"privacyPolicyURL": "https://github.com/jpsweeney97/codex-tool-dev/blob/main/plugins/turbo-mode/decide/PRIVACY.md"`.
raw_findings.proposed_fix: Pick one side and make the two agree. Cheapest: condition the SKILL.md grant on user-named evidence -- e.g. "the repo, the last three decisions, and any calendar or record the user points you at are witnesses this lane is allowed to call" -- which brings it inside PRIVACY's existing "any artifact, path, or evidence the user names". Otherwise widen PRIVACY's read list to name calendar or connector-served personal records, and say whether reading one can leave the machine.

raw_findings.title: Four non-plugin skills outcome-shaping routes to are undocumented as plugin dependencies, while the one comparable external route is qualified

The README's own summary sentence -- "Each member routes to its neighbors by name and stops at its boundary" -- reads as if the routing graph closes inside the plugin, which for this member it does not.
